title: HubSpot Chatbot vs an AI Sales Agent: What the Free Bot Does, What HubSpot AI Chat Costs, and When to Add One
summary: What the free HubSpot chatbot does, what HubSpot's AI customer agent costs, and when a website AI sales agent is worth adding. A Storylane breakdown.
body_markdown:
If you run a website on HubSpot, you already own a chatbot. HubSpot's chatbot builder is free, it lives inside the same chat widget your team uses for live chat, and it writes everything it collects straight into your CRM. Most of the threads ranking for "hubspot chatbot" today are Reddit and HubSpot Community posts asking the same three questions: what does the free bot actually do, what does the AI version cost, and is it enough?


Here is the position I will defend: **the free HubSpot chatbot is a good router, HubSpot's AI customer agent is a good support resolver, and neither is built to sell your product to a first-time visitor who has a real question.** If your website's job is to turn anonymous traffic into qualified meetings, that last job is where a dedicated AI sales agent earns its place. If it is not, stay on HubSpot and save the money.


I'm Madhav, CMO at Storylane. We sell an AI sales agent (RepX), so I have a bias, and I will flag it where it matters. Every HubSpot plan name, feature limit and price below was checked on hubspot.com on October 8, 2026. HubSpot changes packaging often, so verify on their pricing page before you buy.


## What the HubSpot chatbot actually is


In HubSpot, a "chatbot" is a rule-based bot you build inside a chatflow. You pick a template, drag in actions in a visual editor, and decide which questions it asks and where each answer goes. HubSpot describes the free builder as a way to "qualify leads, book meetings, provide customer support, and scale your one-to-one conversations," with no coding required.


What the free builder gives you, per HubSpot's chatbot builder page:


- Templates organized by goal (qualify leads, book meetings, answer common support questions).
- A visual editor to write your own questions and copy.
- Personalization from CRM contact data, and two-way sync so anything the bot collects lands on the contact record.
- Meeting booking and lead qualification inside the chat window.
- Handoff to a live agent, plus automations such as creating tickets, adding contacts to lists and workflows, and triggering an email sequence after a conversation closes.


The important word is **rule-based** . The bot follows the path you drew. It does not read your website, understand an open-ended question, or improvise an answer. HubSpot itself draws this line on its customer agent page: traditional chatbots "follow decision trees and break on unexpected questions."


## What you get free vs what needs a paid HubSpot plan


The builder is free on every plan, but several of the features people assume are included sit behind Professional. HubSpot's knowledge base article on creating bots and the Service Hub pricing page list these limits:


Capability Free Starter Professional / Enterprise


Chatbot builder (chatflows with a bot) Yes Yes Yes


Conversational bots feature level "Limited features" "Limited features" "Additional features"


Live chat branding Includes HubSpot branding Remove HubSpot branding Remove HubSpot branding


If/then branches in a bot No No Yes


Knowledge base search and the knowledge base and support bot template No No Service Hub Professional or Enterprise


AI customer agent No No Professional or Enterprise, billed in HubSpot Credits


That if/then row is the one that surprises people. HubSpot's own documentation states that Starter and free users cannot add if/then branches. Without branching, a "qualification bot" is really a fixed questionnaire: every visitor gets the same sequence regardless of how they answer. You can still collect fields and offer a meeting link, but you cannot route an enterprise visitor differently from a student without moving up a tier.


## HubSpot AI chatbot: the customer agent


When people search "hubspot ai chatbot," what HubSpot sells today is its **customer agent** . It is a different product from the rule-based bot. Per HubSpot's product page, it answers in natural language, is trained on your knowledge base, website, CRM data and past conversations, can take actions in your CRM, and hands off to your team with context. It works across chat, email, social (WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger) and inbound calls.


Two things to notice before you treat it as a website sales agent:


1. **It is positioned as a support agent.** HubSpot's page title is "AI Customer Agent for Customer Support," and conversations are tracked in the help desk. The outcome it is priced on is a resolved conversation.
2. **It can count lead qualification as a resolution.** HubSpot's FAQ says "a resolution can also occur if customer agent qualifies a lead." So it can do some inbound qualification, but the product is designed and measured around deflecting and resolving questions, not around running discovery or showing your product.


If your main question is how far the customer agent can stretch into inbound sales, we cover that in detail in[HubSpot's customer agent for inbound sales](https://www.storylane.io/blog/hubspot-customer-agent-inbound-sales) .


## HubSpot chatbot pricing, as shown on hubspot.com today


HubSpot prices by hub, tier and seat, with different rates for annual and monthly billing, and prices vary by region and currency. Check the live[HubSpot pricing page](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/service) for your numbers; the table below shows where chat and AI features sit by tier.


Plan (Service Hub) Price Credits Chat and AI relevance


Free Free None listed Rule-based bot builder, live chat with HubSpot branding


Starter Paid, per seat Included allowance Remove HubSpot branding; bots still "limited features," no if/then branches


Professional Paid, per seat; onboarding fee listed Included allowance If/then branches, knowledge base bots, customer agent


Enterprise Paid, per seat; talk to sales Included allowance Everything in Professional plus advanced routing


Then the AI layer on top:


- **Customer agent:** HubSpot's FAQ states it is "priced per conversation resolved, at $0.50 per resolution." A resolution means the agent provided support and the conversation was not handed to a human for 72 hours, or the agent qualified a lead.
- **HubSpot Credits:** the customer agent runs on credits. Paid plans include a monthly allowance (above), and additional credits can be bought in packs or pay-as-you-go (see the[HubSpot pricing page](https://www.hubspot.com/pricing/service) ). You can set spend controls per feature.
- **Trial:** the Service Hub pricing page currently offers 14 days of unlimited customer agent use when you buy at least one Service Professional or Enterprise seat.


Marketing Hub has its own pricing, and the chatbot builder appears across Marketing, Sales, Service and Content Hub. The practical takeaway: the free bot costs nothing, but the features that make a bot smart (branching, knowledge base answers, the AI agent) start at Professional.


## The real question: router, resolver, or seller?


Most "HubSpot chatbot vs X" debates go wrong because they compare features instead of jobs. A website chat widget can do three different jobs, and each needs a different tool.


Job What it looks like Best fit


Router Ask two or three questions, send sales visitors to a meeting link and support visitors to a ticket Free HubSpot chatbot (Professional if you need branching)


Resolver Answer how-to and account questions from your help center so tickets never reach a human HubSpot customer agent


Seller Answer product, pricing-model and competitor questions from a first-time visitor, show the product, qualify on fit, and book the right meeting Dedicated website AI sales agent


The router job is cheap and the free bot does it well. The resolver job is what HubSpot built the customer agent for. The seller job is different because a buyer's questions are not in your help center. They ask "does this work with our stack," "how is this different from the tool we use now," and "can I see it." A decision tree cannot answer those, and a support agent trained on your help docs is not tuned to run discovery. For a broader look at that distinction, see[chatbots vs AI agents](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chatbots-vs-ai-agents) .


## Where the free HubSpot bot wins


- **Cost and speed.** It is free, and a simple meeting-booking bot can go live the same day.
- **Native CRM data.** Contact properties, lists and workflows are right there. No integration to maintain.
- **Predictability.** A rule-based bot says exactly what you wrote. For regulated industries or tight brand rules, that is a feature.
- **Low-intent or low-volume sites.** If your site gets little sales traffic, or your buyers already know what they want, a router is all you need.


If those describe you, do not buy anything else. Spend the effort on fast follow-up instead:[lead response time](https://www.storylane.io/blog/what-is-speed-to-lead) usually matters more than how clever the widget is.


## Where it falls short for demand gen


Demand gen and web teams usually hit the same walls:


- **Open-ended questions dead-end.** When a visitor types something the tree did not anticipate, the bot falls back to "talk to sales" or a form. That is a form with extra steps.
- **Branching costs a tier.** Routing by company size, use case or region needs if/then branches, which need Professional.
- **It cannot show the product.** The bot can drop a link, but it cannot walk a visitor through the product in the conversation.
- **The AI option is built for support.** The customer agent is measured and billed on resolutions, which aligns with deflecting support volume. That is a fine incentive for a help desk and an awkward one for a sales conversation, where the goal is a qualified meeting, not a closed ticket.


Buyers who reach a website chat commonly ask about pricing, integrations, how a product compares to what they use today, and whether they can see it before talking to anyone. Those are sales questions, and they decide whether a visitor books.


## An illustrative worked example


**The numbers below are hypothetical, chosen only to show the math.** Plug in your own.


Say your site gets 400 chat conversations a month that start on pricing, product or comparison pages. Today the free HubSpot bot routes them: 25% book a meeting via the link, the rest leave or drop into a form.


- Free bot: 400 x 25% = 100 meetings booked, at $0 in software cost.
- Customer agent: if you are already on Service Hub Professional and it resolves 200 of those conversations, that is 200 x $0.50 = $100 in resolution fees, paid from credits. But "resolved" means the visitor got an answer and did not need a human. It does not mean they booked.
- Dedicated AI sales agent: the question to model is not cost per conversation. It is how many more of the 400 turn into qualified meetings. If a sales agent lifted booking from 25% to 30% (hypothetical), that is 20 more meetings a month. Whether that pays depends on your meeting-to-pipeline rate and deal size, not on the chat price.


The lesson: price chat tools on the outcome you care about. Support teams care about resolutions. Demand gen teams care about qualified meetings. For how vendors structure that pricing, see[AI sales agent pricing models](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ai-sales-agent-pricing-models) .


## When a dedicated AI sales agent is worth adding


Add one when most of these are true:


1. **Your high-intent pages get meaningful traffic** (pricing, product, comparison, integration pages), and visitors leave without booking.
2. **Your buyers ask product questions before they will talk to sales.** If chat transcripts are full of "does it do X," a router is leaving value on the table.
3. **Your product is easier to understand when you see it.** Showing beats telling for most B2B software.
4. **You need qualification that adapts** , not the same five questions for every visitor.
5. **You want to keep HubSpot as the system of record.** A good sales agent should push qualified leads and conversation summaries into HubSpot rather than replace it.


You do not have to rip anything out. A common setup is to keep the HubSpot widget for support and logged-in customers, and run the AI sales agent on marketing pages. How to split that routing cleanly is covered in[routing an AI agent on a HubSpot website](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ai-agent-hubspot-website-routing) .


## Where Storylane RepX fits (full disclosure)


RepX is Storylane's AI agent for your website. It answers, qualifies and books meetings with visitors in real time. What I can point to on the[RepX product page](https://www.storylane.io/repx) today:


- **Answers with the product, not just text.** RepX pulls up relevant interactive demos during the conversation and walks the visitor through the real product. That is the main difference from both HubSpot options.
- **Trained on your material.** Website, docs, decks, call scripts and interactive demos.
- **Qualifies on your criteria.** You define your ICP in plain English, and it asks discovery questions (pain, current setup, timeline).
- **Books meetings** , or drives signups and trials if that is your goal.
- **Guardrails** on what it will and will not say about pricing, competitors and compliance.
- **Text, voice and video** conversation modes.
- **Sends qualified leads and conversation summaries to HubSpot** , Salesforce and Slack.


What RepX is not: a help desk or a support resolver. If your chat volume is mostly existing customers with account questions, HubSpot's customer agent is the more natural fit. RepX pricing is not listed on our public plans page, so talk to us for a quote rather than relying on a number in a blog post.


## How to decide in one afternoon


1. **Export last quarter's chat transcripts** from HubSpot conversations and tag each by intent: support, sales question, routing only.
2. **If routing dominates,** stay on the free bot. Upgrade to Professional only if you need branching.
3. **If support dominates,** trial the customer agent (HubSpot currently offers 14 days with a Service Professional or Enterprise seat) and measure resolutions.
4. **If sales questions dominate,** pilot an AI sales agent on your three highest-intent pages and measure qualified meetings per conversation against the free bot.
5. **Keep one source of truth.** Whatever you choose, make HubSpot the place meetings and qualification data land, and measure them there.


## Common mistakes


- **Assuming the free bot has branching.** It does not on Free or Starter.
- **Treating "resolved" as "converted."** A resolution is a support metric.
- **Forgetting the onboarding fee and seat minimums** when budgeting a Professional upgrade.
- **Running two bots on the same page.** Decide which widget owns which pages.
- **Buying on cost per conversation.** Buy on meetings, pipeline and the quality of the handoff.


## Bottom line


The HubSpot chatbot is free, native and good at routing. HubSpot's AI customer agent is a capable support resolver that costs Professional plus $0.50 per resolution. Neither is designed to sell your product to a new visitor. If your website is a demand gen asset and your visitors ask real product questions, a dedicated AI sales agent that shows the product and books qualified meetings into HubSpot is worth testing. If not, keep the free bot and fix your follow-up speed first.

## FAQ


### Is the HubSpot chatbot free?


Yes. HubSpot's chatbot builder is available on the free plan with no credit card. Some features, such as if/then branches and knowledge base bots, require a Professional or Enterprise subscription, and the free live chat widget includes HubSpot branding.


### Does HubSpot have an AI chatbot?


Yes. HubSpot's AI option is its customer agent, which answers in natural language using your knowledge base, website and CRM data. It requires a Professional or Enterprise edition and runs on HubSpot Credits.


### How much does the HubSpot AI chatbot cost?


HubSpot's customer agent is priced at $0.50 per resolved conversation, paid with HubSpot Credits, on top of a Professional or Enterprise subscription. Professional seat prices vary by billing term and region, so check HubSpot's pricing page for current numbers.


### Can the free HubSpot chatbot qualify leads and book meetings?


Yes. It can ask qualifying questions, save answers to the CRM and offer a meeting link. On Free and Starter it cannot use if/then branches, so every visitor follows the same path.


### Should I replace the HubSpot chatbot with an AI sales agent?


Usually you add rather than replace. Keep HubSpot chat for support and customers, and run an AI sales agent on high-intent marketing pages, with leads and summaries flowing into HubSpot.
